BCD-01.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of contingency planning controls to help ensure resilient Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) (e.g., Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) or Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) playbooks).
BCD-01.title: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)

BCD-01.1.description: Mechanisms exist to coordinate contingency plan development with internal and external elements responsible for related plans.
BCD-01.1.title: Coordinate with Related Plans

BCD-01.2.description: Mechanisms exist to coordinate internal contingency plans with the contingency plans of external service providers to ensure that contingency requirements can be satisfied.
BCD-01.2.title: Coordinate With External Service Providers

BCD-01.3.description: Mechanisms exist to redeploy personnel to other roles during a disruptive event or in the execution of a continuity plan.
BCD-01.3.title: Transfer to Alternate Processing / Storage Site

BCD-01.4.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate recovery operations in accordance with Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs).
BCD-01.4.title: Recovery Time / Point Objectives (RTO / RPO)

BCD-01.5.description: Mechanisms exist to define specific criteria that must be met to initiate Business Continuity / Disaster Recover (BC/DR) plans that facilitate business continuity operations capable of meeting applicable Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs).
BCD-01.5.title: Recovery Operations Criteria

BCD-01.6.description: Mechanisms exist to communicate the status of recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities to designated internal and external stakeholders.
BCD-01.6.title: Recovery Operations Communications

BCD-01.7.description: Mechanisms exist for process owners to establish and maintain formal Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) plans to ensure information is detailed enough, accurate and representative of current operations in order to sustain and/or restore operations under adverse conditions.
BCD-01.7.title: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) Plans

BCD-02.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and document the critical Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that support essential missions and business functions.
BCD-02.title: Identify Critical Assets

BCD-02.1.description: Mechanisms exist to resume all missions and business functions within Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) of the contingency plan's activation.
BCD-02.1.title: Resume All Missions & Business Functions

BCD-02.2.description: Mechanisms exist to continue essential missions and business functions with little or no loss of operational continuity and sustain that continuity until full system restoration at primary processing and/or storage sites.
BCD-02.2.title: Continue Essential Mission & Business Functions

BCD-02.3.description: Mechanisms exist to resume essential missions and business functions within an organization-defined time period of contingency plan activation.
BCD-02.3.title: Resume Essential Missions & Business Functions

CHG-01.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of a change management program.
CHG-01.title: Change Management Program

CHG-02.description: Mechanisms exist to govern the technical configuration change control processes.
CHG-02.title: Configuration Change Control

CHG-02.1.description: Mechanisms exist to prohibit unauthorized changes, unless organization-approved change requests are received.
CHG-02.1.title: Prohibition Of Changes

CHG-02.2.description: Mechanisms exist to appropriately test and document proposed changes in a non-production environment before changes are implemented in a production environment.
CHG-02.2.title: Test, Validate & Document Changes

CHG-02.3.description: Mechanisms exist to include a cybersecurity and/or data protection representative in the configuration change control review process.
CHG-02.3.title: Security, Compliance & Resilience Representative for Asset Lifecycle Changes

CHG-02.4.description: Automated mechanisms exist to implement remediation actions upon the detection of unauthorized baseline configurations change(s).
CHG-02.4.title: Automated Security Response

CHG-02.5.description: Mechanisms exist to govern assets involved in providing cryptographic protections according to the organization's configuration management processes.
CHG-02.5.title: Cryptographic Management

CHG-03.description: Mechanisms exist to analyze proposed changes for potential security impacts, prior to the implementation of the change.
CHG-03.title: Security Impact Analysis for Changes

CHG-04.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce configuration restrictions in an effort to restrict the ability of users to conduct unauthorized changes.
CHG-04.title: Access Restriction For Change

CHG-04.1.description: Mechanisms exist to perform after-the-fact reviews of configuration change logs to discover any unauthorized changes.
CHG-04.1.title: Automated Access Enforcement / Auditing

CHG-04.2.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent the installation of software and firmware components without verification that the component has been digitally signed using an organization-approved certificate authority.
CHG-04.2.title: Signed Components

CHG-04.3.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce a two-person rule for implementing changes to critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).
CHG-04.3.title: Dual Authorization for Change

CRY-01.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of cryptographic protections controls using known public standards and trusted cryptographic technologies.
CRY-01.title: Use of Cryptographic Controls

CRY-01.1.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to prevent unauthorized disclosure of information as an alternative to physical safeguards.
CRY-01.1.title: Alternate Physical Protection

CRY-01.2.description: Mechanisms exist to address the exporting of cryptographic technologies in compliance with relevant statutory and regulatory requirements.
CRY-01.2.title: Export-Controlled Cryptography

CRY-01.3.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of information during preparation for transmission and during reception.
CRY-01.3.title: Pre/Post Transmission Handling

CRY-01.4.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to conceal or randomize communication patterns.
CRY-01.4.title: Conceal / Randomize Communications

CRY-01.5.description: Mechanisms exist to identify, document and review deployed cryptographic cipher suites and protocols to proactively respond to industry trends regarding the continued viability of utilized cryptographic cipher suites and protocols.
CRY-01.5.title: Cryptographic Cipher Suites and Protocols Inventory

CRY-02.description: Automated mechanisms exist to enable systems to authenticate to a cryptographic module.
CRY-02.title: Automated Authentication Through Cryptographic Modules

CRY-03.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality of data being transmitted.
CRY-03.title: Transmission Confidentiality

CRY-04.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to protect the integrity of data being transmitted.
CRY-04.title: Transmission Integrity

CRY-05.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to prevent unauthorized disclosure of data at rest.
CRY-05.title: Encrypting Data At Rest

CRY-05.1.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive/regulated data residing on storage media.
CRY-05.1.title: Storage Media

CRY-05.2.description: Mechanisms exist to remove unused data from online storage and archive it off-line in a secure location until it can be disposed of according to data retention requirements.
CRY-05.2.title: Offline Storage

IAC-01.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of identification and access management controls.
IAC-01.title: Identity & Access Management (IAM)

IAC-01.1.description: Mechanisms exist to retain a record of personnel accountability to ensure there is a record of all access granted to an individual (system and application-wise), who provided the authorization, when the authorization was granted and when the access was last reviewed.
IAC-01.1.title: Retain Access Records

IAC-01.2.description: Mechanisms exist to strictly govern the use of Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) solutions, both on-premises and those hosted by an External Service Provider (ESP).
IAC-01.2.title: Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA)

IAC-01.3.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a current list of authorized users and service accounts.
IAC-01.3.title: User & Service Account Inventories

IAC-02.description: Mechanisms exist to uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) organizational users and processes acting on behalf of organizational users.
IAC-02.title: Identification & Authentication for Organizational Users

IAC-02.1.description: Mechanisms exist to require individuals to be authenticated with an individual authenticator when a group authenticator is utilized.
IAC-02.1.title: Group Authentication

IAC-02.2.description: Automated mechanisms exist to employ replay-resistant authentication.
IAC-02.2.title: Replay-Resistant Authentication

IAC-02.3.description: Mechanisms exist to accept and electronically verify organizational Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials.
IAC-02.3.title: Acceptance of PIV Credentials

IAC-02.4.description: Mechanisms exist to implement Out-of-Band Authentication (OOBA) under specific conditions.
IAC-02.4.title: Out-of-Band Authentication (OOBA)

IAC-03.description: Mechanisms exist to uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) third-party users and processes that provide services to the organization.
IAC-03.title: Identification & Authentication for Non-Organizational Users

IAC-03.1.description: Mechanisms exist to accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials from third-parties.
IAC-03.1.title: Acceptance of PIV Credentials from Other Organizations

IAC-03.2.description: Automated mechanisms exist to accept Federal Identity, Credential and Access Management (FICAM)-approved third-party credentials.
IAC-03.2.title: Acceptance of Third-Party Credentials

IRO-01.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and govern processes and documentation to facilitate an organization-wide response capability for cybersecurity and data protection-related incidents.
IRO-01.title: Incident Response Operations

IRO-02.title: Incident Handling

IRO-02.1.description: Automated mechanisms exist to support the incident handling process.
IRO-02.1.title: Automated Incident Handling Processes

IRO-02.2.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and govern an insider threat program.
IRO-02.2.title: Insider Threat Response Capability

IRO-02.3.description: Automated mechanisms exist to dynamically reconfigure system components as part of the incident response capability.
IRO-02.3.title: Dynamic Reconfiguration

IRO-02.4.description: Mechanisms exist to identify classes of incidents and actions to take to ensure the continuation of organizational missions and business functions.
IRO-02.4.title: Incident Classification & Prioritization

IRO-02.5.description: Mechanisms exist to coordinate with approved third-parties to achieve a cross-organization perspective on incident awareness and more effective incident responses.
IRO-02.5.title: Correlation with External Organizations

IRO-02.6.description: Mechanisms exist to automatically disable Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), upon detection of a possible incident that meets organizational criteria, which allows for forensic analysis to be performed.
IRO-02.6.title: Automatic Disabling of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

IRO-03.description: Mechanisms exist to define specific Indicators of Compromise (IOC) to identify the signs of potential cybersecurity events.
IRO-03.title: Indicators of Compromise (IOC)

IRO-04.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain and make available a current and viable Incident Response Plan (IRP) to all stakeholders.
IRO-04.title: Incident Response Plan (IRP)

IRO-04.1.description: Mechanisms exist to address data breaches, or other incidents involving the unauthorized disclosure of sensitive or regulated data, according to applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations.
IRO-04.1.title: Data Breach

IRO-04.2.description: Mechanisms exist to regularly review and modify incident response practices to incorporate lessons learned, business process changes and industry developments, as necessary.
IRO-04.2.title: IRP Update

MON-01.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of enterprise-wide monitoring controls.
MON-01.title: Continuous Monitoring

MON-01.1.description: Mechanisms exist to implement Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (IDS / IPS) technologies on critical systems, key network segments and network choke points.
MON-01.1.title: Intrusion Detection & Prevention Systems (IDS & IPS)

MON-01.10.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor deactivated accounts for attempted usage.
MON-01.10.title: Deactivated Account Activity

MON-01.11.description: Automated mechanisms exist to implement pre-determined corrective actions in response to detected events that have security incident implications.
MON-01.11.title: Automated Response to Suspicious Events

MON-01.2.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM), or similar automated tool, to support near real-time analysis and incident escalation.
MON-01.2.title: Automated Tools for Real-Time Analysis

MON-01.3.description: Mechanisms exist to continuously monitor inbound and outbound communications traffic for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions.
MON-01.3.title: Inbound & Outbound Communications Traffic

MON-01.4.description: Mechanisms exist to generate, monitor, correlate and respond to alerts from physical, cybersecurity, data protection and supply chain activities to achieve integrated situational awareness.
MON-01.4.title: System Generated Alerts

MON-01.5.description:
Mechanisms exist to monitor wireless network segments for:
(1) Rogue wireless devices; and
(2) Anomalous and/or hostile activities.
MON-01.5.title: Wireless Network Monitoring

MON-01.6.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize Host-based Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (HIDS / HIPS) to actively alert on or block unwanted activities and send logs to a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM), or similar automated tool, to maintain situational awareness.
MON-01.6.title: Host-Based Devices

MON-01.7.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a File Integrity Monitor (FIM), or similar change-detection technology, on critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to generate alerts for unauthorized modifications.
MON-01.7.title: File Integrity Monitoring (FIM)

MON-01.8.description: Mechanisms exist to review event logs on an ongoing basis and escalate incidents in accordance with established timelines and procedures.
MON-01.8.title: Security Event Monitoring

MON-01.9.description: Mechanisms exist to log all Internet-bound requests, in order to identify prohibited activities and assist incident handlers with identifying potentially compromised systems.
MON-01.9.title: Proxy Logging

PRI-01.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation and operation of data protection controls throughout the data lifecycle to ensure all forms of Personal Data (PD) are processed lawfully, fairly and transparently.
PRI-01.title: Data Privacy Program

PRI-01.1.description: Mechanisms exist to appoints a Chief Privacy Officer (CPO) or similar role, with the authority, mission, accountability and resources to coordinate, develop and implement, applicable data privacy requirements and manage data privacy risks through the organization-wide data privacy program.
PRI-01.1.title: Chief Privacy Officer (CPO)

PRI-01.10.description: Mechanisms exist to strictly govern financial incentives offered to data subjects for Personal Data (PD) to ensure compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
PRI-01.10.title: Financial Incentives For Personal Data (PD)

PRI-01.11.description: Mechanisms exist to limit the collection, receiving, processing, storage, transmission, sharing, updating and/or disposal of Personal Data (PD) according to reasonable consumer expectations for what is necessary and proportionate.
PRI-01.11.title: Reasonable Data Privacy Practices

PRI-01.2.title: Privacy Act Statements

PRI-01.3.title: Dissemination of Data Privacy Program Information

PRI-01.4.description:
Mechanisms exist to appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO):
(1) Based on professional qualifications; and
(2) To be involved in all issues related to how Personal Data (PD) is collected, received, processed, stored, transmitted, shared, updated and/or disposed.
PRI-01.4.title: Data Protection Officer (DPO)

PRI-01.5.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and manage Binding Corporate Rules (BCR) (e.g., data sharing agreement) to legally-bind all parties engaged in a joint economic activity that contractually states enforceable rights on data subjects with regard to the processing of their personal data.
PRI-01.5.title: Binding Corporate Rules (BCR)

PRI-01.6.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure Personal Data (PD) is protected by logical and physical security safeguards that are sufficient and appropriately scoped to protect the confidentiality and integrity of the PD.
PRI-01.6.title: Security of Personal Data (PD)

PRI-01.7.description: Mechanisms exist to limit the disclosure of Personal Data (PD) to authorized parties for the sole purpose for which the PD was obtained.
PRI-01.7.title: Limiting Personal Data (PD) Disclosures

PRI-01.8.description:
Mechanisms exist to appoint an individual to determine the following criteria about Personal Data (PD):
(1) The purpose why PD is necessary; 
(2) Authorized methods to collect, receive, process, store, transmit, share, update and/or dispose PD; and
(3) Authorized parties PD may be shared with.
PRI-01.8.title: Data Fiduciary

PRI-01.9.description: Mechanisms exist to assign accountability to a Personal Data Process Manager, or equivalent role, to ensure Personal Data (PD) is collected, received, processed, stored, transmitted, shared, updated and/or disposed of according to data subject consent.
PRI-01.9.title: Personal Data (PD) Process Manager

TPM-01.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of third-party management controls.
TPM-01.title: Third-Party Management

TPM-01.1.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a current, accurate and complete list of External Service Providers (ESPs) that can potentially impact the Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability and/or Safety (CIAS) of the organization's Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).
TPM-01.1.title: Third-Party Inventories

TPM-02.description: Mechanisms exist to identify, prioritize and assess suppliers and partners of critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) using a supply chain risk assessment process relative to their importance in supporting the delivery of high-value services.
TPM-02.title: Third-Party Criticality Assessments

TPM-03.description:
Mechanisms exist to:
(1) Evaluate security risks and threats associated with Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) supply chains; and
(2) Take appropriate remediation actions to minimize the organization's exposure to those risks and threats, as necessary.
TPM-03.title: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM)

TPM-03.1.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize tailored acquisition strategies, contract tools and procurement methods for the purchase of unique Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).
TPM-03.1.title: Acquisition Strategies, Tools & Methods

TPM-03.2.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize security safeguards to limit harm from potential adversaries who identify and target the organization's supply chain.
TPM-03.2.title: Limit Potential Harm

TPM-03.3.description: Mechanisms exist to address identified weaknesses or deficiencies in the security of the supply chain
TPM-03.3.title: Processes To Address Weaknesses or Deficiencies

TPM-03.4.description: Mechanisms exist to develop and implement a spare parts strategy to ensure that an adequate supply of critical components is available to meet operational needs.
TPM-03.4.title: Adequate Supply

TPM-04.description: Mechanisms exist to mitigate the risks associated with third-party access to the organization's Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).
TPM-04.title: Third-Party Services

TPM-04.1.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct a risk assessment prior to the acquisition or outsourcing of technology-related Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).
TPM-04.1.title: Third-Party Risk Assessments & Approvals

TPM-04.2.description: Mechanisms exist to require External Service Providers (ESPs) to identify and document the business need for ports, protocols and other services it requires to operate its Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).
TPM-04.2.title: External Connectivity Requirements - Identification of Ports, Protocols & Services

TPM-04.3.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure that the interests of external service providers are consistent with and reflect organizational interests.
TPM-04.3.title: Conflict of Interests
